clue.text: An opening in the bank?

parts.note: reads like a hole in a river bank, but means the cash dispenser set into the outside of a bank building

explanation.walkthrough: The 'bank' is a financial one: the British nickname for a cash machine describes the gap in the bank's wall where it sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash machine built into a bank's outer face is literally a gap in its masonry, hence the colloquial name.

clue.text: Immediately at the scene of the action

definitions.text: at the scene of the action
definitions.meaning: physically present where things are happening

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both instantly and present at the very place where events unfold.

clue.text: Girl holding notice to get out of the way

indicators.note: the girl's name grips the other piece within it

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A girl clutching a notice is told to step aside.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to move out of the path of something, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Send out round the East for what's required

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the compass point
out suggests the letters of send are put out of order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Dispatch something around the eastern region to meet its needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns SEND into NEDS, and 'round' puts E inside to give NE-E-DS.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessities are the things that are required, so the plural noun matches the phrase.

clue.text: Chief's line with different maps for use at night

parts.note: a chief is the head

indicators.note: different signals that the letters of maps are made into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A leader's line of different maps is meant for night-time use.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the clue describes what the lamps are for rather than naming them, and 'different' signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicle lights at the front are switched on in darkness, so the definition describes their purpose.

clue.text: Firm friends?

parts.note: firm friends usually means loyal pals, but here it means companions at the same firm or company

explanation.definitionFit: Colleagues at the same company are the friends one makes through a firm, a cryptic reading of the phrase.

clue.text: Plunging in with a worn piece of cloth

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the word plunging

explanation.surface: Diving in wearing a piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a cloth wrapped round the waist, worn in South Asia, so it is a garment of cloth.

clue.text: Mad comic with union movement is out of touch with audience

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters of mad comic and union are moved around

explanation.surface: An unhinged comedian joining a union campaign loses contact with the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held without means of communication is unable to reach anyone, cut off from contact.

clue.text: Note progress with new building

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
development is progress or growth

explanation.surface: A memo reports progress on the construction of a new building.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebuilding an area with fresh construction is the planning term for new building work.

clue.text: Ace with stunt almost comes to grief — the fool!

indicators.note: coming to grief means being wrecked, so these letters are scrambled
almost means the last letter of stunt is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: An ace pilot's stunt goes wrong, and he is called a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts STUNT to STUN; 'comes to grief' shuffles ACE and STUN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy or foolish person is slangily called this, so it serves as a synonym for fool.

clue.text: Order a s-stove

parts.note: the stammered s-stove signals a stuttered synonym: a stove is a range, stammered by repeating its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone stammers while asking for a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 's-stove' imitates a stutter, so the synonym for stove, RANGE, is stuttered too, giving R-RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order is to organise them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Live in very large house finally, like a fat cat?

indicators.note: the word for live goes in the size abbreviation

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of house

explanation.surface: Living in a huge house in the end, like a wealthy fat cat.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'fat cat' is a rich businessman, but the definition reads it literally as an overweight cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A literally fat cat would be grossly overweight, which is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Celebrate when Les and Simone are hitched

indicators.note: hitched suggests the two names are joined and blended together

explanation.surface: A wedding is celebrated when Les and Simone get married.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform a ceremony formally, such as a wedding, is to celebrate it.

clue.text: Vehicle moved aimlessly

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a small motorcycle, and the verb means wandered around in a dejected way.

clue.text: City lived in turmoil; it's a downward slope

indicators.note: turmoil means confusion, so the letters of city and lived are mixed up

explanation.surface: A city lived in chaos as it slid downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a downward incline, from the Latin for sloping down.

clue.text: As arranged, I'm seated with second cup of coffee

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Once settled in my seat, I have a second cup of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup used for strong black coffee, from the French for half-cup.

clue.text: Southern salesmen picked up in phone distribution

indicators.note: the reversed pieces go inside the word for phone

parts.note: to dial is to phone

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means read upwards, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: reps are sales representatives

explanation.surface: Southern salesmen are collected for a phone distribution campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'picked up' reads upwards, turning the southern salesmen round as one unit before they go into the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading things widely is distribution, a noun synonym.

clue.text: What the Babes did in panto for a tree

parts.note: the Babes sat, as they did in the story
taken as written
the pantomime Babes in the Wood, a British Christmas show, supplies the wood

explanation.surface: In the pantomime, the Babes did something to a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Babes in the Wood is a traditional British pantomime about two children lost in a forest, so the Babes sat in the wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinwood is a tropical tree with a lustrous yellow timber.

clue.text: Are they carried by conductors?

parts.note: suggests musical conductors carrying cases of notes, but means wallets for banknotes carried by bus conductors

explanation.walkthrough: Old British bus conductors collected fares and carried wallets for paper money.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallets for paper money hold bank notes, so conductors handling fares would carry them.

clue.text: The centre of hottest backing for the fight

indicators.note: backing means the selected letters are read backwards
the centre of a word is all of it except its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The hottest part of the heat backs the fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of HOTTEST is OTTES; 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief brawl or argument is a scrap, the hyphenated noun for a fight.

clue.text: Ravine covered in black stuff — a dye

indicators.note: covered in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: coal is black fuel
a chine is a deep ravine, especially on the Isle of Wight or Dorset coast

explanation.surface: A gorge coated with black material yields a dye.
explanation.walkthrough: A chine is a southern English word for a narrow coastal ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson colouring made from crushed insects, used to colour food.

clue.text: Class of actors for the listener

indicators.note: for the listener means the word is heard, not written

parts.note: the cast is the group of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A class of actors performing for a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid social rank or hereditary class is called this, as in the Hindu system.

clue.text: Plant out of bed in a short line

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the shortened word
short means the last letter of line is cut off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
up means risen, out of bed

explanation.surface: A plant out of its bed in a short row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests a flowerbed for the plant, but 'out of bed' simply means risen; 'short' clips the line.
explanation.definitionFit: The lupin is a garden flower with tall spikes, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Forward or return note

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards or back

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A note that goes forward or back.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical note worth half a semibreve has this name, called a half note in America.

clue.text: Tidy up to hospital's delight

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: trim means neat or tidy
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Tidying up the hospital brings delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyful laughter and merriment are a form of delight.

clue.text: Cashier to treat as unworthy

definitions.meaning: to cashier is to discharge someone from service, usually the armed forces
to brush aside as not worth considering

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to sack someone and to reject a matter as not worth attention.

clue.text: Gem, we hear, round in pocket

indicators.note: we hear means the word sounds like the gem's name

parts.note: a pearl is a gem
O is round in shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gem, so we hear, rounded up in someone's pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: PURL (a knitting stitch) sounds like PEARL.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket something is to steal it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Double-sided type found in print

parts.note: suggests printers' type printed on both sides, but means a two-faced character from a novel

explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's novella features a man with a good and an evil self, a printed character of two sides.
